clue.text: Taking a break from work quietly when in some disorder

indicators.note: letters left in some disorder are jumbled, so the job word and the quiet letter are rearranged together

parts.note: a posting is a job or appointment, a piece of work one is sent to
P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly

explanation.surface: Someone slips off work without a fuss while the office is in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-style indirect anagram: 'work' must first become POSTING, and with P added the letters POSTINGP are put 'in some disorder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Halting or pausing an activity is the same as taking a break from it.

clue.text: A scholar's holding motorists up, being a crawler

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole assembled piece is read from bottom to top
holding means one piece clasps the other inside it

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a scholar, and the possessive adds S
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motorists' organisation

explanation.surface: An academic is stalling the drivers behind, crawling along.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British breakdown and motoring association. 'Motorists up' tempts a solver to turn only RAC round, but 'up' works on the whole assembly, and the leading 'A' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle sacred in ancient Egypt, it is a crawling insect.

clue.text: Neat crossing in the city

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a single neat is an ox
a ford is a shallow river crossing

explanation.surface: Tidy road crossings in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A university city on the Thames is an example of a city.

clue.text: Hand over here and now!

definitions.meaning: in attendance, at this current moment

explanation.surface: Someone demands an object be passed over immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow or give formally is one sense, and being at hand at this moment is the other.

clue.text: To steal can mean jail

definitions.meaning: slang for a prison or police station

explanation.surface: Theft can land you in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for pinch, and also slang for a prison or police cell.

clue.text: The girl a top journalist failed to see

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried girl, standing for a girl
ED is the editor, the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A young woman whom the chief reporter overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook something or fail to notice it is a past-tense synonym of not seeing it.

clue.text: Opening the first letter

definitions.meaning: coming at the very start, beginning
the opening letter of a name or word

explanation.surface: The start of a document, its opening character.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for coming first, and also a noun for the letter that begins a name.

clue.text: Ancient Greek coasters possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word's letters may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps drink mats from classical Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian philosopher is a famous example of an ancient Greek.

clue.text: Do without to give to others?

definitions.meaning: with 'with', to manage without something, forgo it
to hand out or distribute, as a pharmacist does medicine

explanation.surface: Is it giving things up that means sharing them out?
explanation.definitionFit: Forgoing something (dispensing with it) is one sense, and distributing goods is the other.

clue.text: Sore calf properly treated — exposed to the fresh air

indicators.note: something properly treated is worked on and reshaped, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An injured leg muscle is given the right care, out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: The borrowed Italian phrase describes doing something outdoors, in the open air.

clue.text: There's endless talk about sports equipment

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for talking about is cut off

parts.note: to talk about a subject is to debate or examine it

explanation.surface: Fans never stop chatting about their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavy disc thrown in athletics is a piece of sporting apparatus.

clue.text: Meadowland beyond the river

parts.note: past means beyond, further on than
the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Grassy fields lying on the far side of a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassland used for grazing animals is meadowland.

clue.text: Song-writers serving in HM forces?

definitions.meaning: an air is a tune or song, so composers of airs could whimsically be called ...
members of the Royal Air Force, part of Her Majesty's armed services

explanation.surface: Composers who have joined up in the British military.
explanation.walkthrough: HM is Her (or His) Majesty, the British monarch, so HM forces are the UK armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: Composers of airs or tunes split the word playfully, while flying personnel of the air force fit the second sense.

clue.text: Teasing can get offensive in time

parts.note: offensive behaviour is bad, objectionable
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Ribbing someone can turn nasty given long enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful mocking banter is light teasing conversation.

clue.text: An agitator of a sourer disposition

indicators.note: disposition can mean arrangement, so the letters of the two words are set out anew

explanation.surface: A troublemaker with a rather bitter temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stirs up feeling or rouses people is a type of agitator.

clue.text: Raconteurs who stretch the truth!

definitions.meaning: people who entertain with tales and anecdotes
people who tell fibs, liars, as a child might say

explanation.surface: Anecdote-tellers who exaggerate their tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilled anecdote-tellers fit the first sense, and fibbers are called this in nursery language.

clue.text: Simple means of transport for those lacking balance

definitions.text: Simple means of transport for those lacking balance

parts.words: Simple means of transport for those lacking balance
parts.note: pictures a three-wheeler, which a small child who cannot yet balance on two wheels can ride

explanation.definitionFit: A three-wheeled cycle stays upright on its own, so a rider needs no balance.

clue.text: A member of more than one union? That's criminal!

definitions.text: A member of more than one union? That's criminal!

parts.words: A member of more than one union? That's criminal!
parts.note: union is read not as a trade union but as a marriage, and being wed twice at once is a crime

explanation.definitionFit: Someone married to two spouses at once commits an offence.

clue.text: Peer, resuming management, is to have total control

indicators.note: management means handling and rearranging, so the letters of the two words are reorganised

explanation.surface: A lord takes back the running of the firm and is now the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule with complete authority is to dominate without rival.

clue.text: A small number on the list could well appear outstanding

parts.note: NO is the short form of number
a table is a list of figures or names

explanation.surface: A minor figure on the roster might look remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable or worthy of note is a synonym of outstanding.

clue.text: Mess about and maybe cause great anger

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the two words are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fooling around may make someone furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mad with rage is one sense of the noun, a fit of fury.

clue.text: A woman is getting back brown

indicators.note: getting back means the woman's name and the following word are read backwards together

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lady is returning with a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt or raw, this earth pigment gives a reddish or yellowish brown.

clue.text: Hard as ever in the Dover area

indicators.note: in means the word ever is placed inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: SE is South East, the region of England where Dover lies

explanation.surface: Tough as always down on the Kent coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is a port on England's south-east coast, so its area is SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and hard are synonyms for harsh or demanding.

clue.text: Announcer imbibing a small measure — it's shrewder

indicators.note: imbibing is drinking in, so the measure goes inside the announcer

parts.note: a town crier made public announcements
FT is the abbreviation for foot, a small measure of length

explanation.surface: A broadcaster downs a little drink and becomes more cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOWN CRIER was the official who called out public notices in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more cunning or wily is a comparative synonym of being more shrewd.

clue.text: Plug evil counsel

parts.note: to plug a product is to advertise it, and an ad is an advertisement
vice is wickedness

explanation.surface: Promoting wickedness is bad guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is guidance or recommendations given to someone.

clue.text: A piece of music for the violoncello composed long ago

indicators.note: a piece of means a short run of letters is taken from within the instrument's name

explanation.surface: A tune written for the cello in a bygone age.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly, at some time in the past, is a synonym of long ago.

clue.text: Advances can be arranged by many branches

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, standing for many
the limbs of a tree are its large branches

explanation.surface: Progress can be made by an array of boughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rises or goes upward, as prices or a climber do, is to advance.

clue.text: They feel Article 10 — key article — to be retrogressive

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
ten written as a word

indicators.note: retrogressive means moving backwards, so the key and article that follow are read in reverse

parts.note: E is a musical key
an is again the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A legal clause, the tenth, is a key one that turns out to be backward-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects use their feelers to sense and touch their surroundings.

clue.text: No way-out course!

definitions.meaning: an entrance or right of admission, the opposite of an exit
a dish served at a meal, as the main dish or one before it

explanation.surface: A dead-end path on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word means admission or a way in, and it also names a dish in a meal.

clue.text: Water colour painting

parts.note: read not as a picture done in watercolours but as a picture showing the colours of the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A painting of the ocean depicts water in all its colours.
